comparison.a: Chooses a monolithic CLI (O1) and a thin-slice milestone plan that delivers user-visible output early while deferring convention-dependent features behind configuration. It keeps implementation complexity lower and maps MUST requirements to concrete acceptance tests and exits.
comparison.b: Chooses a plugin architecture (O2) and front-loads a Phase A engine/API build, which increases upfront risk and time-to-first-value for this scoped tool. It is stronger on extensibility and security posture for third-party plugins, but that is not required to reach core closure.

evidence.note: A selects O1 explicitly for lowest complexity and direct coverage of MUST requirements.
evidence.quote: O1 is the lowest-complexity architecture that directly satisfies the core MUST requirements

evidence.note: A’s M1 delivers CLI+ingest+render+emit and gates on AT1–AT6, enabling early closure-ready output.
evidence.quote: exit_criteria": ["AT1–AT6 pass on a fixture dataset.", "Output directory contains only static assets

evidence.note: B’s first phase is core engine/context/plugin API work, delaying delivery of required end-user features.
evidence.quote: Phase A — Core Engine & Plugin Infrastructure

evidence.note: B acknowledges higher upfront complexity and plugin API instability risk inherent to O2.
evidence.quote: Higher upfront complexity designing a stable plugin API and shared data model

payload.notes: For the stated goals (static site generator with search/tags/backlinks) A is more likely to reach an implementable, testable MVP with less architectural risk. B is better if a plugin ecosystem is a primary requirement, which is not established here.
